Definition: from G1537 and G1377; to pursue out, i.e. expel or persecute implacably:--persecute.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to pursue out, to chase away and persecute without rest, and Paul uses it once, for the Jews who killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets and persecuted the apostles. He says they please not God and are contrary to all men, forbidding the gospel to be spoken to the Gentiles. The word is pursuit that never stops, a hatred that follows its victims from town to town.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe persecution is the world's answer to the gospel, because the truth threatens every power that lives by a lie.
